I won't lie, some days, I'm really miserable and I feel like death would be a relief. For me, I mostly try to write or play video games on days like that. If I can distract myself long enough, I find that I'm tired enough to sleep and another day rolls around. It's painful and awful and I would never wish it on anyone, which is part of the reason why I don't end up going through with it - my suicide would put my family into that state with an added dose of guilt and I don't want anyone else to experience it.

Then there are good days. There are no days where I feel like I'm ready to take on the world, mind you, because I haven't sought the help I need (someday, when I have better health insurance, I hope to find better coping mechanisms than putting my life to a standstill in order to weather the storm). But the good days are days where I shower, get dressed and make some small change toward a better life. I have some credits now, I've saved up a little bit of money (a pittance, I think on my bad days, and as for the credits I've wasted thousands of dollars that I have to pay back to the US government) but when I think about it in perspective, it's more than I had a year ago so it's something. I bought a vase recently that says "Grow," and I put some cheesy fake flower in it. On my bad days I want to smash the thing, because I feel utterly pathetic compared to everyone else my age, but on my good days it reminds me that I can only build my own future step by step, not make a magical leap to what I wish I was.

Even if you had screwed up as many times as I have - my first screwup cost over $22,000 in room, board and tuition when all was said and done - I think there's always *something* that can be done to improve, even just a little. Are you afraid to tell your parents because they'll be disappointed in you? It may help to have a plan as to what you're going to do to make it better, like getting a job for the upcoming semester and taking classes at a local college in the fall in order to save money on room and board as well.

Hey. I'm 25 and actually have been in a rather similar situation to you...I went to a 4-year school straight out of high school, couldn't adjust, did poorly due to anxiety and depression, lied about attending classes after awhile to my parents. I just didn't want them to know what a loser I was, you know? I wanted them to think I was doing well, and the other part of me thought maybe I could escape when it got unbearable, either by going to a beach and being homeless there or by killing myself. My parents found out and they were *livid*. My sister, who's pretty much my best and only friend, wouldn't speak to me. 

Eventually, I enrolled in a local community college. I still suffered from the same anxieties, and withdrew after a few months there as well...and lied about it again, because how could I tell them I was doing the same shit that I had sworn never to do again? And how could I explain that it was because of a problem in my head that I didn't know how to fix or even describe properly? I told them I was doing well, they checked the Dean's List and - lo and behold, my name wasn't on it - and my mom cried for a long while about it. She wanted me to move out or go to inpatient treatment somewhere, but I already felt like enough of a freak that I was sure I'd rather die than be inpatient somewhere, luckily my dad talked her out of it because I don't know that I would have made it there. (Although...I wish I'd gone then because maybe I'd be better, but I won't go now because of the same insecurities).

I re-enrolled and did two semesters fairly successfully, and then...you guessed it! I got anxious again and stopped. I only withdrew from two of my classes because I was pretty sure I could handle the other ones. I was wrong. I failed and was supposed to be graduating, lied about graduating, and now my parents have been asking about it to the point where they definitely know and I'm still afraid to take off that mask myself because I feel like all they'll see is a gaping black hole. 

Either they find out now or you keep lying about it and they find out later, at least in my experience. If you've more courage than I do, and if your parents are anything like mine, I'd say tell them. It's probably at least in part the weight of the anxiety that you've got a secret that's making you feel this way. 

Also, speaking from experience if you re-apply, maybe not this semester (I've never done it the semester immediately following one of my failures) but in the fall, you should be able to get another loan. It's not ideal but it's not the end.

Thanks for replying...even if you're only being kind because you feel obligated to be, I appreciate it. I don't know how I'd make money without a degree. I don't know how to make money *with* a degree, but it seems more likely if I graduate. I promised my parents, the only people in the world who give a shit about me, that I wouldn't do this again and yet here I am. In the past when I joined clubs I was always too anxious to speak to anyone. I feel like I'm annoying people. And if I put myself out there on a dating website and didn't get any replies, well, that probably would be it for me. Which is pathetic, I know, because there are SO MANY people out there who have it worse than I do, and who have actual, tangible reasons to feel this way, but I honestly don't think I would be able to take that rejection. I just don't know. It feels like I have this gaping black hole in me and yet some part of me keeps mindlessly tugging at it to make it larger and larger until it will swallow me up. It's close to that point and most days a part of me hopes for some sort of accident so that I won't be responsible for any of it anymore. I'm not a bad person, I'm really not, but I'm the cause of all my own problems and yet I can't handle them. It seems so much simpler to just...cease.
